title: I’m building a 2D game about economy, business and trading, and I’d love your feedback
author: Piotruspro_
selftext:
Hi everyone,

I’ve been working on my own 2D trading and economy game for a while now. I’d like to show it to you and find people who are willing to share their opinions and suggestions that could help the project grow.

![video](8w9nkzpcosvh1)

In short, it’s a game about building your own path in a living city. There is no single way to progress, and it’s not a typical tycoon where you click and watch numbers go up. Decisions and strategy actually matter here.

Here is what you can already do, or what I’m currently working on:

You can drive cars, with their own physics, a gearbox and engine sound.

![video](rzudoqqepsvh1)

You can own an apartment and trade apartments with other players. Inside, you decorate everything your own way with furniture, wallpapers, floors, lighting and extras. There is a furniture store and an edit mode where you can rearrange everything to your taste. You can also trade plots of land and build your own buildings on them.

You can build an industrial business or a farm. It’s not a place and forget system. Animals need to be fed and watered, fields need watering, machines need maintenance, and weather and random events can always shake things up.

You can become a clothing designer. You design patterns at a dedicated tailoring table, sew the clothes and sell whole collections to companies or other players. It pays to follow trends and product prices, because they decide how much you earn on a sale.

You can invest in stocks and cryptocurrencies. The market is shared between players and constantly moving. You can also mine crypto on hardware that you assemble yourself from parts.

You can work toward energy independence. You set up solar panels and wind turbines, run the cabling and store energy in batteries.

You can start your own companies and cryptocurrencies. The idea is that other players can invest in them. You can grow your own coin alone or together with others, for example by accepting it as payment in your shop with a discount. I want to add many more mechanics like this.

You can customize your character with hairstyles, beards, tattoos and accessories, so everyone looks different.

The game is at a very early stage. Some things work well, some are still sketches, and many parts need polishing. That’s exactly why I’m posting here. What matters most to me is that the game includes your ideas too.

I’d love to hear what you feel is missing in games like this, what annoys you about them, and which feature would make you want to keep coming back. Which of the things above sound the most interesting, and which seem unnecessary?

Thanks for reading, and any feedback, even harsh, is very welcome.

[https://discord.gg/99wu3bSxMv](https://discord.gg/99wu3bSxMv) there is a discord where you can share your suggestions and follow the project or you can suggest here on comments Thanks!!

comments.author: Rcraft
comments.body:
my eyes hurt from the visual noise on your video. too much going on, too pixelated for my taste. All of the text is far too small on the screen for anyone watching to make out in your demo videos. Basically, I imagine that most people seeing your videos would be really confused about what it is and will just scroll past it. There's no hook, unless I'm missing something that players of this genre love to see in the first 5 seconds of your video clip or a specific gameplay hook that would intrigue them. I don't see what sets this apart from the crowd in a simple leading thesis - "building your own path in a living city" is a puzzling statement rather than an intriguing one, to me. Think about how someone might take those words. "building your own path" - ok, am i literally building paths? is it a career path? crafting path? "no single way to progress... or watch numbers go up... decisions and strategy matter" - ok, so don't go in expecting these things, that kind of don't really match with the video and vibe of the game. the first two can be made relatively obvious through the video - yea you can walk around and place things, you show the openness, you don't have to double-declare "multiple ways to progress" and can put more descriptive words in place. 

Sorry for the wall of text, hopefully what I'm describing is helpful.
